def add(a,b): return [x+y for x,y in zip(a,b)]
def scale(c,a): return [c*x for x in a]
def mix(x,a0,a1): return add(scale(1-x,a0),scale(x,a1))
def feasible_interval(u0,u1,z,eps):
    xs=[i/10000 for i in range(10001) if abs((1-i/10000)*u0+(i/10000)*u1-z)<=eps+1e-12]
    return None if not xs else (min(xs),max(xs))
def robust_margin(B,R,w,I):
    lo,hi=I; q=[[dot(w,add(B[k],mix(x,R[k][0],R[k][1]))) for x in (lo,hi)] for k in range(len(B))]
    per=[]
    for i in range(len(q)):
        cs=[min(q[i][e]-q[j][e] for e in range(2)) for j in range(len(q)) if i!=j]
        per.append(min(cs) if cs else None)
    if not per or any(v is None for v in per): return q,per,None,None

final_candidate.title: Completion Atlas: Coupling-Robust Current Actions from One Factual Residual
final_candidate.hook: A single factual WAM residual identifies an equivalence class of current-action corrections, not a point update. Completion Atlas executes a newly proposed current suffix only when it wins for every residual-response completion consistent with that residual.
final_candidate.hook_shape_rationale: Shape (b), structural reframe: the abstract of semanticscholar:a77ce57cc8614da8e469228797af4c69274a1428 operationalizes the opposite point-transport assumption by applying one observed-image pseudoinverse correction inside the next flow generation, while Completion Atlas makes the non-identified completion set the controller's primary object. Shape (a) was viable through a predicted reduction in wrong-dominance rate under contact shifts, but rejected because the paper-level contribution is the set-valued estimand and shared-coefficient construction rather than the magnitude of one empirical split.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes when the residual observed after one action retains its direction and scale for a different candidate action, versus when the candidate lies outside action support or invokes a different contact mechanism and must not inherit that residual; this is the unresolved residue of execution-time re-grounding in semanticscholar:a77ce57cc8614da8e469228797af4c69274a1428 and trust-based execution in dblp:journals/corr/abs-2605-06222. — stakes: manipulation users can receive confidently worsened actions after perturbations, while the field lacks conditions under which online WAM correction is causally interpretable rather than accidental.
gap_closure.how_closed: C00 reframes cross-action residual transport as a faithful partial-identification measurement over a coupled residual-response dictionary, and structural_prior_encoding forces factual and current-branch residuals to use the same mixture coefficient so robust action selection has no candidate-only correction path around e_t.

final_candidate.core_mechanism: Freeze an open-weight π0.5 policy and a DreamZero-compatible WAM on LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0, and train one linear terminal-success head g on frozen WAM future latents using those benchmarks' existing success labels; g is then frozen and is also the score used by the ordinary uncorrected WAM-reranking baseline. After executing the previous chunk b_{t-1}, compute the factual residual e_t by concatenating the fixed WAM encoder difference E(o_t)-E(o_pred_t_minus) with proprioceptive error standardized by nonzero training-set coordinate standard deviations, and project it with a training-only PCA map P_d to z_t=P_d e_t, where d=64 by default and is selected from {32,64,128} on held-out factual reconstruction and downstream regret. Training data are matched residual-intervention groups: restore the same pre-prefix LIBERO or RoboTwin2.0 state, execute the same b_{t-1} and the same K current action chunks under different existing simulator mass, friction, contact, and occlusion settings, retain chunks executable in every member of the group, and record both z_n and each branch future-latent residual ΔZ_{nk}=E(o_{n,t+H}^k)-E(o_pred_{n,t+H}^k); K=8 by default and is selected from {4,8,16} on validation success versus latency. Fit a coupled atlas with M=32 atoms, selected from {16,32,64}, where factual signatures are columns u_m of U and each atom has a small candidate-conditioned response map R_m(φ_{nk}) from frozen WAM trajectory features φ_{nk}; every training bundle has one simplex coefficient λ_n and reconstructs both z_n≈Uλ_n and ΔZ_{nk}≈Σ_m λ_{nm}R_m(φ_{nk}). The atlas loss adds a matched-pair contrast term of weight β=1, selected from {0.5,1,2}, requiring the observed difference in branch residuals between two residual interventions to equal the difference produced by their shared coefficients; groups enter this term only when their observed branch difference exceeds τ_Δ, defined as the maximum duplicate-rollout encoder noise on a held-out deterministic duplicate set, so any correction that ignores λ_n has strictly positive contrast loss and cannot be a zero-loss solution on the retained responsive groups. At deployment, no λ point estimate or hidden physical parameter is inferred: the observed residual defines the completion set Λ_t={λ∈Δ_M: ||Uλ-z_t||_∞≤ε_e}, with ε_e=median(r_e)+c_e MAD(r_e) on validation reconstruction residuals, c_e=2 by default and selected from {1,2,3} on validation wrong-dominance versus fallback rate. For every newly sampled executable current candidate a_t^k, each λ∈Λ_t induces a corrected future Z_k(λ)=Z_pred_k+Σ_m λ_mR_m(φ_k) and affine frozen score q_k(λ)=g(Z_k(λ),language); there is no learned marginal-residual score and no pairwise-ranking supervision. Compute the coupling-robust dominance margin Γ_t=max_i min_{j≠i} min_{λ∈Λ_t}[q_i(λ)-q_j(λ)] by linear programs; execute the corresponding current candidate only when Λ_t is nonempty and Γ_t>0, otherwise execute the uncorrected π0.5 current top candidate for the smallest native controller interval and replan, never an action stored from an obsolete state. Conditional on the true branch correction sharing some atlas coefficient in Λ_t and on the frozen linear head being the declared decision score, Γ_t>0 certifies only score dominance over all admissible completions—not task success or real-physics coverage—and candidates outside the atlas convex-hull support necessarily take the current-action fallback. For each candidate d, fit P_d only on training-group factual residuals before computing any z_n, and define H as the endpoint of the current candidate chunk rather than a tuned horizon; define each validation r_e as min_{lambda in Delta^M} ||U lambda-z||_infinity before computing epsilon_e.
final_candidate.core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES LEDGER
P1: residual-responsive contact or observation mismatches recur with similar joint factual/branch signatures across randomized LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 episodes — untested — falsification target; without recurrence the completion set is empty or too broad and the method falls back.
P2 observation-model: matched groups use the same pre-prefix simulator state, previous chunk, and candidate chunks while varying only named simulator perturbations, then condition the estimand on the intersection of candidates executable in every group member; this is controlled but selection-biased toward intersection support and is not claimed unbiased for unseen real physics.
P3: a finite convex atlas can approximate the joint residual-response family at the chosen encoder and horizon — untested — falsification target; validation reconstruction and oracle-singleton controls test this approximation rather than assuming it.
P4: the frozen linear success head g preserves the task ordering relevant to the benchmark proposal distribution — untested — falsification target; all formal dominance language is therefore explicitly about g, while task success is empirical.
ESTIMAND: for a deployment residual z and current candidate features φ_k, the target is the identified set 𝒟_k(z,φ_k)={Σ_m λ_mR_m(φ_k): λ∈Δ_M, ||Uλ-z||_∞≤ε_e} of branch future-latent corrections over the randomized-simulator, π0.5-candidate, intersection-support process, not a conditional mean, physical-parameter posterior, centered candidate residual, or pairwise preference.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
The runnable naive version predicts one point correction ΔZ_point_k=f(e_t,φ_k) and reranks current candidates once; branch (i) fails because one factual residual generally admits several incompatible cross-action response completions, so a point decoder silently chooses an unidentified coupling. Completion Atlas confronts that failure by retaining every atlas completion consistent with e_t through action selection, and the shared λ plus matched residual-intervention contrast makes ignoring e_t incompatible with zero atlas loss on residual-responsive groups. STANDARD-TOOL FOLLOW-UP: partial identification and robust optimization are textbook objects, but textbook set-membership control assumes a specified state-space disturbance set or parameter class; here the set itself must be learned as a coupled high-dimensional factual/video-residual atlas whose same coefficient is observed on the factual side and missing on VLA-generated current branches, with no physical parameter semantics and a new online candidate set each cycle.
BLOCK 3 — DESIGN RATIONALE
The anchor is kept single because the coupled completion set already supplies its own causal fidelity test and current-action decision rule; a separate ranking-diagnostic leg would repeat the prior composition without changing the mechanism. Point residual dynamics, GP correction, Bayes/dual system identification, importance weighting, robust tube MPC over hand-given disturbances, and a direct outcome scorer were rejected because they regress to occupied lineage nodes or select one transport rather than preserving the non-identified completion set; CarrierLock, Boundary Score, GISS-2x2, ExitReplay, and ScaffoldFracture are also avoided because no persistent carrier, boundary functional, skill graph, censoring replay, or fixed scaffold is constructed. Under the allowed fulltext-degraded evidence, the mechanism-level boundaries are abstract-level: FWM guides a diffusion policy with a feedback world model, FBFM injects one observed-image pseudoinverse into active flow generation, ReDRAW fits point latent-state residual dynamics, Twin Rollouts fixes a shared-noise branch coupling, and ordinary WAM reranking scores one point future, whereas Completion Atlas learns no action correction outside the e_t-constrained completion set and optimizes worst-case current-candidate dominance over that whole set. JMDP constructs coupled transition processes, CF-GPS abducts exogenous noise for counterfactual policy search, CG-World contributes a world-state dataset/protocol, and WorldSample improves a policy from world-model samples; Completion Atlas instead freezes policy/WAM and neither infers a latent physical state nor trains a policy, while its claimed delta from CoCo is specifically retention of every factual-consistent coupling through selection rather than commitment to one constructed coupling—an abstract-level boundary requiring primary-text verification because the allowed CoCo cache exposes no method and therefore is not positive novelty evidence.
final_candidate.core_mechanism_steps:
1. Freeze π0.5 and the DreamZero-compatible WAM, choose the fixed encoder E, and train then freeze the linear success head g from existing LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 terminal labels; inputs are predicted future latents and language, and output is the common baseline score used by every reranking arm.
2. Generate matched residual-intervention groups by restoring one pre-prefix simulator state, varying named built-in physics/occlusion settings, executing the same b_{t-1}, and retaining K action chunks executable across the group; inputs are simulator states and π0.5 chunks, and outputs are paired current observations, WAM predictions, and rollback snapshots.
3. Compute e_n, z_n=P_d e_n, each candidate feature φ_{nk}, and each branch future-latent residual ΔZ_{nk} by executing every retained current chunk from its own post-prefix snapshot; these branch outcomes are training/evaluation data only and are never queried online.
4. Fit U, {R_m}, and per-bundle λ_n jointly with factual reconstruction, branch reconstruction, and matched residual-intervention contrast losses; the shared-coefficient code path outputs one coupled factual/branch atlas, and the contrast term makes a λ-ignoring response incur nonzero loss on every retained responsive group.
5. Select d, M, K, β, and c_e on disjoint validation groups using factual/branch reconstruction, wrong-dominance, benchmark success, fallback, and latency, then freeze U, {R_m}, P_d, g, the VLA, and WAM.
6. At deployment after the previous chunk finishes, compute the new real residual z_t and solve the feasibility LP for Λ_t; its input is only the just-observed factual residual and the frozen factual atoms, and its output is a set of admissible coefficients rather than a point latent-state or physics estimate.
7. Sample K newly executable π0.5 suffixes from the current observation, run the frozen WAM once per suffix, and evaluate R_m(φ_k) for all atoms; the output is one affine corrected-future family Z_k(λ) per current candidate, with no replay of the obsolete previous action.
8. Solve the pairwise robust-dominance LPs analytically from q_k(λ), compute Γ_t, and either execute the robustly dominant current suffix or the current uncorrected π0.5 fallback for one native controller interval; this set optimization directly changes the physical action selected.
9. Log Γ_t, completion-set diameter, support/fallback decisions, task success, rollback top-1 regret, and latent error, then replan from the next real observation; the same logs support the residual-signature permutation and oracle-singleton controls without changing the deployed algorithm. Before Step 3, fit each candidate PCA map P_d on training-group e_n only, and take H to be the endpoint of the current candidate chunk; in Step 5 compute r_e per validation sample as min_{lambda in Delta^M} ||U lambda-z||_infinity. If fewer than two executable current suffixes are available in Step 7, skip Gamma_t, use the current uncorrected pi0.5 fallback for one native controller interval, and use the frozen policy's native deterministic tie-break for fallback ties.
final_candidate.falsification_prediction: Run frozen π0.5 plus the same DreamZero-compatible WAM and linear head on existing LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 rollback tasks with scripted mass, friction, contact, and occlusion perturbations, comparing uncorrected WAM reranking, FBFM, ReDRAW-style point residual prediction, a point-decoded version of the same atlas, and Completion Atlas on identical current-candidate bundles. If the mechanism works, wrong-dominance rate and rollback top-1 regret decrease while closed-loop task success increases, especially on bundles where multiple atlas coefficients fit the same factual residual. The named load-bearing variable is Γ_t, the worst-completion dominance margin; as a negative control, permute factual signatures u_m across their branch-response atoms before constructing Λ_t while keeping candidates, scores, and atlas capacity fixed, which should drive downstream regret and task success toward the uncorrected baseline rather than merely alter Γ_t. An oracle-singleton control that reveals the training-only branch-compatible λ supplies an upper bound, while failure of the permutation to erase the gain kills the claim that factual-residual coupling—not generic robust reranking—caused the improvement.
final_candidate.compute_budget: Approximately 32 A100-40GB GPU-days plus simulator CPU time for matched rollback generation, frozen-WAM feature extraction, atlas training, validation, and three-seed evaluation; with four available A100-40GB GPUs this is roughly eight fully utilized GPU-days and is comfortable within five months. The campaign uses only open weights and existing simulators, so estimated paid API cost is $0.
